q: Separation of crude oil takes place in a ______ into different fractions in an oil refinery.
e: The process occurs in a fractional distillation column as per the textbook.

q: In fractional distillation, the fractions condense and come out of the column at different heights depending on their ______.
e: Boiling point determines where each fraction condenses in the column.

q: The petroleum gas fraction comes out first at the top of the column because its molecules have the ______.
e: Low boiling point allows gases to rise and condense at the top.

q: The residue at the bottom of the fractional distillation column is used to make bitumen for ______.
e: Bitumen is used for road surfacing as stated in the textbook.

q: All the fractions from crude oil distillation are insoluble in water and ______ in air.
e: The textbook notes all fractions burn in air.

q: Petrol (gasoline) has an approximate boiling point range of ______ °C.
e: Table 8.1 lists petrol’s boiling range as 35–75°C.

q: Kerosene (paraffin) is used as a fuel for ______.
e: Kerosene is listed as jet fuel in Table 8.1.

q: Lubricating oil contains approximately ______ carbon atoms per molecule.
e: Table 8.1 shows lubricating oil has 19–35 carbon atoms.

q: Fuel oil is used as a fuel for ships, factories and ______.
e: Fuel oil is used for central heating as per Table 8.1.

q: Refinery gas is used as bottled gas for gas cookers and ______.
e: Refinery gas powers motor cars and cookers according to Table 8.1.

q: Naphtha is primarily used to make ______.
e: Naphtha’s main use is in petrochemical production (Table 8.1).

q: Diesel oil has an approximate boiling point range of ______ °C.
e: Table 8.1 gives diesel’s boiling range as 250–340°C.

q: Bitumen is a black substance used to make surface roads and ______.
e: Bitumen is used for both road surfacing and roofing.

q: The fraction with the smallest molecules is ______.
e: Refinery gas has 1–4 carbon atoms, the fewest among fractions.

q: The most viscous fraction from crude oil distillation is ______.
e: Bitumen is the residue and is described as not flowing easily—most viscous.
